text.arabic_uthmani: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَتَيَآ أَهْلَ قَرْيَةٍ ٱسْتَطْعَمَآ أَهْلَهَا فَأَبَوْا۟ أَن يُضَيِّفُوهُمَا فَوَجَدَا فِيهَا جِدَارًۭا يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ فَأَقَامَهُۥ ۖ قَالَ لَوْ شِئْتَ لَتَّخَذْتَ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًۭا

words.gloss_range: sequential-resumptive connector launching the resumed travel after the prior ultimatum
words.prose: The opening {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) resumes the strained agreement from (18:76) as immediate movement. Because it is fused to the departure verb, the ayah does not open a detached scene; it turns the boundary condition into a third journey panel, echoing the earlier departures at (18:71) and (18:74) while shifting from dialogue back into exterior action. Its clipped onset also makes the restart sound abrupt, not leisurely.

topics.headline: fused sequential resumption
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins by converting the previous ultimatum into immediate resumed motion, not by resetting the scene.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the particle a sequential connector attached to the departure clause.

topics.headline: sequence, cause, and resumption together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the connector carries both nextness and consequence, so the journey continues under the pressure of (18:76).
topics.reason: The particle senses are locally compatible with continuation after the prior boundary.

topics.headline: third journey-panel launcher
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated episode-opening pattern that makes this wall scene the third panel of the travel tests.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows connect this opening to the travel-panel pattern at (18:71) and (18:74).

topics.headline: clipped restart sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the quick onset as part of the ayah’s abrupt restart into motion.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a concrete sound payoff that matches the immediate narrative restart.

words.gloss_range: completed dual self-propelled departure opening the third incident
words.root_gloss_range: release and unbinding range, locally narrowed to self-initiated movement in Form VII
words.prose: {{ar:ٱنطَلَقَا}} ({{tr:inṭalaqā}}) keeps Musa and al-Khiḍr grammatically joined in a completed dual departure. Its Form VII shape makes the movement self-propelled, a release into the next test rather than a sending by someone else, while the repeated departure formula links the wall episode to the earlier panels at (18:71) and (18:74). The release-root also lets the restart sit in ironic contrast with the town’s closed refusal and al-Khiḍr’s unpaid generosity, and the firm emphatic sound gives the renewed movement a decisive push.

topics.headline: dual completed self-propelled departure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both travelers remain one grammatical pair at the restart, before later singular repair splits agency.
topics.reason: The perfect dual Form VII is directly licensed by QAC morphology and the repeated dual verb chain.

topics.headline: release-root pressure in travel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the departure as renewed unbinding into the test, with generosity pressure kept as irony rather than the selected sense.
topics.reason: V4 root range supports release and open-handedness, but local Form VII selects departure while retaining contrastive color.

topics.headline: episode-opening travel formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the exact travel verb as a structural marker that completes the three-incident pattern.
topics.reason: Contextual rows tie the form to the repeated Moses-al-Khiḍr panel openings at (18:71), (18:74), and (18:77).

topics.headline: firm restart sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the firm consonantal push as part of the decisive restart after threatened separation.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a concrete acoustic payoff tied to the travel verb.

words.gloss_range: terminative threshold particle beginning the long temporal scene-frame
words.prose: {{ar:حَتَّىٰٓ}} ({{tr:ḥattā}}) stretches the journey toward a threshold, and together with the next adverb it opens the familiar until-when frame of the three incidents. The endpoint is not only temporal; it gathers the arrival, request, refusal, discovery, and repair into one long scene whose answer may be felt as delayed until the repair. Its drawn-out recitational shape suits that suspended threshold.

topics.headline: until-when threshold frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that travel is held open until the town encounter becomes the next test.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the particle as opening the temporal frame that governs the following scene.

topics.headline: endpoint with purposive pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the town arrival as both the endpoint of travel and the purposeful doorway to the wall episode.
topics.reason: The broader particle range supports endpoint and purpose, while local syntax selects temporal endpoint.

topics.headline: three-episode frame repetition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same threshold construction structuring the ship, boy, and wall incidents.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows explicitly connect the construction to the repeated frames at (18:71) and (18:74).

topics.headline: lengthened threshold sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the phrase slow at the threshold before the town scene unfolds.
topics.reason: The phonetic row ties long open sounds to the threshold function.

words.gloss_range: realized temporal-conditional adverb introducing the arrival situation
words.prose: {{ar:إِذَآ}} ({{tr:idhā}}) makes the arrival a realized when-scene, not a hypothetical possibility. It keeps the narrative in third-person scene-framing after the prior direct confrontation, and its answer-position remains elastic enough for several actions to unfold inside one condition: arrival, request, refusal, discovery, and repair.

topics.headline: realized condition frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the town episode is presented as an accomplished situation, not a mere possibility.
topics.reason: QAC marks a temporal adverb, and attachment evidence places it inside the governing temporal scene.

topics.headline: when and given-that pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that time-marking and condition-triggering work together in the social test.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows preserve both temporal and conditional force without contradiction.

topics.headline: return from confrontation to narration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the rupture of direct address being folded back into narrated dual action.
topics.reason: Boundary rows track the shift from (18:76) direct confrontation into story-mode scene framing.

words.gloss_range: completed dual arrival directed at the people as object
words.root_gloss_range: coming, arriving, bringing, and performing; locally arrival to people is selected while action/giving pressure survives as irony
words.prose: {{ar:أَتَيَآ}} ({{tr:atayā}}) completes the movement opened by the departure and takes the people as its direct object, so the pair comes to a community, not merely to a location. The dual ending keeps both travelers synchronized, while the root’s giving and action range creates irony: they reach people from whom giving will be refused. The arrival-and-finding field also contrasts with (18:65), where finding led to a divinely given servant.

topics.headline: dual arrival at people
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both travelers arrive as a pair and that the object is the people themselves.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the verb a perfect dual governing the following people noun directly.

topics.headline: arrival with giving-action irony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the arrival root carry a secondary irony of giving and social action without replacing the local sense of coming.
topics.reason: The V4 range is broader than the local arrival sense, so the extra pressure survives only as qualified irony.

topics.headline: access point into social test
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices arrival as the hinge from travel into encounter and as a contrast with the discovery-gift pattern at (18:65).
topics.reason: Contextual rows make the arrival root part of Surah 18 access and discovery scenes.

words.gloss_range: construct people noun as arrival target and social body
words.root_gloss_range: belonging, inhabitants, and qualification; locally inhabitants are selected with moral fitness pressure
words.prose: {{ar:أَهْلَ}} ({{tr:ahla}}) is the construct head in the people-of-town phrase, so the travelers are directed toward a social body before the place itself is named. The word means inhabitants, yet its qualification range matters because the same group will fail the hospitality role implied by belonging to a settlement. Its later repetition turns one community from destination into petition target, and the short people-word opening into the fuller settlement-word lets the phrase sound like movement from social body to domain.

topics.headline: construct arrival target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that people, not geography, stand first as the object of arrival.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as accusative object of arrival and construct head with the following settlement noun.

topics.headline: belonging with qualification pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the inhabitants belong to the place but prove unfit for the hospitality role their identity implies.
topics.reason: V4 supports inhabitants and qualification; local syntax selects inhabitants while the refusal activates the evaluative range.

topics.headline: repeated community pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same community is grammatically tested twice, first by arrival and then by request.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows explicitly tie word 6 to the repeated people noun at word 9.

topics.headline: people-to-place sound shift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the short people noun open into the fuller settlement noun, matching the construct movement.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a concrete sound-form payoff for the construct phrase.

words.gloss_range: indefinite settlement as the people’s domain
words.root_gloss_range: gathering, settlement, receiving, and hospitality-related pressure; locally an unnamed inhabited settlement is selected
words.prose: {{ar:قَرْيَةٍ}} ({{tr:qaryatin}}) keeps the town unnamed and indefinite, so the focus falls on conduct rather than geography. As genitive domain under the people noun, the place is introduced through its community. The settlement-root pressure is pointedly ironic: a gathering-place whose field touches hospitality refuses to gather the two travelers in, and the same surah has already used settlement language in a judgment context at (18:59). The final tanwīn leaves the town audibly open-ended as an unspecified moral setting.

topics.headline: indefinite genitive settlement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the town is unnamed and subordinated to its people, not presented as a famous locality.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as genitive indefinite in construct, and the tanwīn supports non-specific reference.

topics.headline: gathering-place hospitality irony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the irony of a settlement, a gathering domain, failing to receive guests.
topics.reason: V4 supports settlement and gathering-related hospitality pressure, while local sense remains an inhabited settlement rather than an etymological pun alone.

topics.headline: moral settlement discourse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this unnamed town joining a wider Quranic and Surah 18 pattern of settlements as moral communities, including (18:59).
topics.reason: Contextual rows connect the noun to settlement-discourse and local judgment patterns.

topics.headline: indefinite nasal closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the tanwīn leave the town open-ended and unspecified.
topics.reason: The phonetic row links the ending sound to indefiniteness.

words.gloss_range: completed dual Form X request to be fed
words.root_gloss_range: taste, eating, food, and feeding; locally seeking to be fed is selected
words.prose: {{ar:ٱسْتَطْعَمَآ}} ({{tr:istaṭʿamā}}) is more specific than generic asking: Form X makes both travelers seek to be fed. The food itself is recoverable but omitted, so the grammar foregrounds the people being asked and the bodily dependence of the pair. This rare requestative form turns the town scene into a concrete hospitality test, reversing food-giving formulas and recalling Surah 18’s earlier food concern at (18:19). Its emphatic and guttural sounds thicken the mouth-feel of a word about eating and need.

topics.headline: completed dual food request
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both travelers actually make the request before the refusal, with the food object left implicit.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the verb a perfect dual request governing the town’s people.

topics.headline: taste-eat-feed field in Form X
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees need, eating, and social feeding converge in a single requestative verb.
topics.reason: V4 lexical range supports taste, eating, and feeding, and the local Form X selects seeking to be fed.

topics.headline: unique requestative hospitality rupture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that food is uniquely staged as requested and then denied, setting up the immediate refusal.
topics.reason: Distributional and contextual rows mark the Form X occurrence as rare and link it to the request-refusal sequence.

topics.headline: heavy mouth-feel of need
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the emphatic and guttural sounds thicken a word about food and bodily need.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a specific sound payoff tied to the food request.

words.gloss_range: the town’s own people as object of the food request
words.root_gloss_range: belonging, inhabitants, and qualification; locally town-bound inhabitants are selected
words.prose: {{ar:أَهْلَهَا}} ({{tr:ahlahā}}) ties the petition directly back to the unnamed town through its feminine suffix. The asked group is not a random household or kin circle but the settlement’s own inhabitants, so responsibility is civic and social. The repetition from the earlier people noun tightens the test: the same people first receive arrival and then receive need.

topics.headline: suffix-bound petition target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the suffix keeps the people tied to the same town while making them object of the food request.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun with a feminine suffix referring back to the settlement and as object of the request.

topics.headline: inhabitants over kinship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the failure as a town-social failure, not a family scene.
topics.reason: The suffix and antecedent select inhabitants from the broader people/kin range.

topics.headline: destination becomes need-target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated community noun changing governors from arrival to petition.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows explicitly compare the first and second people forms.

words.gloss_range: adversative-sequential connector from request to refusal
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the refusal both the next event and the opposite of the expected hospitality response. The clipped connector and following glottal onset turn a food request into an abrupt social rupture.

topics.headline: immediate contrary result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that refusal is not loosely reported; it follows directly as the jarring answer to the food request.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence license the connector as contrastive sequence between request and refusal.

topics.headline: then-but connective force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees nextness and opposition working together at the rupture point.
topics.reason: The particle’s local force preserves both sequence and adversative contrast.

topics.headline: petition-to-rupture hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the connector as the hinge where hospitality expectation breaks.
topics.reason: The topical rows identify the particle as the pivot from petition to refusal.

topics.headline: abrupt refusal onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the clipped connector move into a hard onset at the negative turn.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a concrete acoustic marker of abrupt refusal.

words.gloss_range: plural perfect of willful refusal by the community
words.root_gloss_range: refusal, aversion, and pride; locally active refusal is selected, not inability
words.prose: {{ar:أَبَوْا۟}} ({{tr:abaw}}) shifts from the two needy travelers to a plural refusing subject, making the town’s response collective. The verb means willful refusal rather than inability, and its pride-laden field makes the refusal morally charged; the structural echo with refusal formulas such as (2:34) colors the scene without importing that whole episode. The denial of hospitality then balances against al-Khiḍr’s unsolicited repair.

topics.headline: collective refusing subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the refusal belongs to the community as a plural actor, not one isolated host.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as third masculine plural perfect after the dual request.

topics.headline: willful pride-charged refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the town’s answer as active aversion, not mere incapacity.
topics.reason: V4 lexical evidence supports refusal with negative evaluative force.

topics.headline: refusal answered by repair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah’s central reversal: people refuse to give, while al-Khiḍr later gives repair unasked.
topics.reason: Contextual rows pair the refusal with the wall repair and with later explanatory pressure.

topics.headline: hard arrest of refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the glottal onset sharpen the shutdown after the request.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a sound payoff aligned with refusal.

words.gloss_range: subordinating particle making hosting the refused complement
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) turns the following hosting verb into the act refused. The denied object is therefore not merely the travelers as persons but the social act of hosting them, compressed into a rapid complement after the refusal verb. The nasal particle also binds audibly into the hosting verb, making refusal-to-host feel like one tight grammatical unit.

topics.headline: hosting as refused complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the refusal targets the act of hosting, made grammatically explicit by the complement particle.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the following subjunctive clause as the content complement of refusal.

topics.headline: verbal-noun duty frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the unrealized hosting action as a social duty converted into the object of refusal.
topics.reason: The particle’s nominalizing and purposive pressure fits the local complement structure.

topics.headline: compressed refusal-to-host unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how quickly the clause packages the social offense.
topics.reason: The topical row treats the infinitival phrase as a compressed full clause.

topics.headline: nasal binding into hosting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the particle bind into the hosting verb as one refusal unit.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a concrete sound connection between particle and verb.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive Form II hosting verb with plural hosts and dual guests
words.root_gloss_range: guesting, hosting, bringing near, and social incorporation; locally full guest-treatment is selected
words.prose: {{ar:يُضَيِّفُوهُمَا}} ({{tr:yuḍayyifūhumā}}) packs the whole failed hospitality relation into one word: the plural townspeople would host the two travelers, but the action remains subjunctive under refusal. Form II makes the denied act full guest-treatment, not casual reception, and the root’s guest/host reciprocity makes the refusal social and spatial: the travelers incline toward protection, but the town refuses to bring them near. Variant readings show a lighter causative or direct-address possibility, while the standard narration keeps Musa’s later direct address reserved for al-Khiḍr; its doubled sound also thickens the denied act of active hosting.

topics.headline: plural hosts and dual guests packed together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one verb preserves both sides of the failed relation: many hosts and the two specific travelers.
topics.reason: QAC marks the subjunctive verb with plural subject agreement and a dual object suffix.

topics.headline: guest-root reciprocity denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the town refuses not food alone but the social incorporation encoded by the hospitality root.
topics.reason: V4 lexical evidence supports guest, host, bringing-near, and reciprocal hospitality pressure.

topics.headline: rare intensive hosting verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the distributional weight of the rare verbal hospitality form appearing exactly where hosting is refused.
topics.reason: Distributional rows identify the verbal hospitality use as rare and narratively charged.

topics.headline: geminated hosting weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the doubled sound thicken the denied act of full hospitality.
topics.reason: The phonetic and variant rows give a concrete sound contrast for the standard Form II reading.

words.gloss_range: sequential connector from refusal to wall discovery
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) moves immediately from refusal to discovery without pausing to explain or condemn the town. The juxtaposition does the judging: after communal rejection, attention relocates to a vulnerable wall inside the same settlement, keeping the ayah’s rapid action-chain intact. The short connector keeps the discovery beat clipped rather than reflective.

topics.headline: bare sequence after refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the narrative proceeds from refusal to discovery with no inserted commentary.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the connector as sequential narrative progression.

topics.headline: sequence by juxtaposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the particle lets adjacency carry evaluation rather than adding explicit judgment.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL lexical row preserves the particle’s bare sequence payoff.

topics.headline: social rejection to wall focus
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the scene pivot from people to object while staying inside the same town.
topics.reason: The topical rows identify this connector as the refusal-to-wall hinge.

topics.headline: clipped discovery pace
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the short connector maintain the rapid chain of actions.
topics.reason: The phonetic row supports the clipped pace payoff.

words.gloss_range: completed dual finding of the wall
words.root_gloss_range: finding, existence, and experience; locally encountered discovery is selected
words.prose: {{ar:وَجَدَا}} ({{tr:wajadā}}) keeps both travelers inside the perception event: they both encounter the wall, but only al-Khiḍr will repair it. No search is narrated, so the verb makes the wall appear as a sudden found object that becomes narratively present and eventually provokes speech. This finding motif belongs to Surah 18’s journey-discovery pattern, including (18:69), (18:86), and (18:93), where what is found or expected to be found is not immediately exhausted by first perception.

topics.headline: dual discovery before singular action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both travelers see the wall before agency narrows to one repairer.
topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect dual finding verb in the continuing dual chain.

topics.headline: finding as encountered presence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the wall become present as an encountered object, not a searched-for target.
topics.reason: The root range includes finding, existence, and experience; local narration selects encountered discovery.

topics.headline: Surah 18 discovery motif
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices finding as a journey method: objects are encountered before their meaning is disclosed.
topics.reason: Contextual rows connect this root to repeated Surah 18 finding scenes and speech responses.

words.gloss_range: locative phrase binding the wall to the same town
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) routes the reader back to the town and places the wall inside the same social domain that refused hospitality. By putting the locative phrase before the wall, the ayah keeps the hostile settlement in view as the vulnerable object appears, so the later repair benefits the very place that rejected the travelers.

topics.headline: town-bound locative suffix
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wall is inside the same unnamed town, not in a new scene.
topics.reason: QAC marks a locative preposition with feminine suffix referring back to the settlement.

topics.headline: town as social container
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the town as the container for both refusing people and vulnerable wall.
topics.reason: The prepositional relation supports the container-domain payoff.

topics.headline: place before object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that location is foregrounded before the wall is named.
topics.reason: The topical row notes the locative phrase preceding the found object.

words.gloss_range: indefinite exposed wall as newly found object
words.root_gloss_range: walling, standing, raised surface, and worthiness; locally a vulnerable freestanding wall is selected
words.prose: {{ar:جِدَارًۭا}} ({{tr:jidāran}}) enters as an indefinite object of finding: an unnamed wall whose importance is not yet disclosed. The word selects an exposed wall rather than a garden enclosure, making vulnerability to collapse fitting. Its root-field of standing, raised surface, and worthiness makes the object more than scenery, and its later explanatory return at (18:82) shows why this wall carries high narrative load. The compact hard consonants give the wall a felt solidity even while the next words expose its instability.

topics.headline: new object of finding
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wall is introduced as new information and as the object that will receive repair.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as indefinite accusative direct object of finding.

topics.headline: exposed worthy wall
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the wall as a vulnerable freestanding structure whose standing matters.
topics.reason: V4 supports wall, worthiness, and raised-surface pressure; local sense selects a physical wall.

topics.headline: rare wall with later reprise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this is a loaded object designed for explanation at (18:82).
topics.reason: Contextual and distributional rows connect this wall to its same-surah explanatory return.

topics.headline: solid consonantal texture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the compact hard sounds match a solid object even as collapse threatens it.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows give a concrete sound-shape payoff.

words.gloss_range: imperfect will/tendency assigned to the wall
words.root_gloss_range: seeking, wanting, intending, and directed tendency; locally metaphorical collapse-tendency is selected
words.prose: {{ar:يُرِيدُ}} ({{tr:yurīdu}}) shifts from completed actions into an ongoing state: the wall is described as wanting to collapse. The inanimate subject is routed by grammar and adjacency, so the wording personifies structural instability without requiring literal consciousness. The root’s seeking-to-intending range lets the wall’s danger feel like a directed tendency, and that apparent will anticipates the later explanation of hidden intentions across (18:79), (18:80), (18:81), and (18:82). The repeated y-sound links this wanting verb to the following collapse verb as one audible tendency.

topics.headline: ongoing wall tendency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the break from completed narrative actions into a present process attached to the wall.
topics.reason: QAC marks an imperfect verb whose 3ms subject is locally recovered as the wall.

topics.headline: personified directed instability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees collapse as a vivid tendency assigned to the wall, not a flat statement of condition.
topics.reason: V4 supports wanting and seeking; local inanimate grammar narrows this to metaphorical structural tendency.

topics.headline: present wanting before hidden intent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the wall’s apparent intention preparing for the later sequence of explained intentions at (18:79), (18:80), (18:81), and (18:82).
topics.reason: Contextual rows link the wanting root and wall root to the explanation arc.

topics.headline: sound link to collapse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the repeated initial sound bind wanting to the following collapse verb.
topics.reason: The phonetic row names the concrete sound relation between the two verbs.

words.gloss_range: subordinating particle making collapse the wanted complement
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) embeds the collapse as the object of the wall’s wanting. The danger is therefore not narrated as a separate event; it is held inside a state predicate as imminent tendency. A variant purpose-passive reading shows how close the phrase can come to purpose, but the standard keeps internal tendency in control. The nasal link also carries the particle into the collapse verb, so the subordination is heard as well as parsed.

topics.headline: collapse as wanted complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that collapse is subordinated under the wall’s wanting rather than made an independent event.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the following subjunctive as complement of the wanting verb.

topics.headline: infinitive-purpose pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the standard complement frame with a nearby purpose-pressure exposed by variant evidence.
topics.reason: Variant evidence is useful contrast, but local canonical syntax keeps the complement under wanting.

topics.headline: embedded danger clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wall’s danger is grammatically delayed and internalized before repair.
topics.reason: The topical row describes the clause architecture as embedding collapse inside a state predicate.

topics.headline: nasal link to collapse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the particle bind audibly into the collapse verb.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a concrete sound connection.

words.gloss_range: dependent Form VII self-collapse of the wall
words.root_gloss_range: undoing, collapse, untwisting, and covenant-breaking; locally autonomous structural collapse is selected
words.prose: {{ar:يَنقَضَّ}} ({{tr:yanqaḍḍa}}) makes the wall’s collapse dependent on the preceding particle and wanting verb, not an independent completed fall. Form VII internalizes the failure: the wall is coming apart on its own rather than being demolished by an outside agent. The root’s undoing image, including covenant-breaking uses such as (2:27) and (13:25), lets physical collapse answer the social breach of hospitality, while variant readings sharpen the standard form’s self-collapse. The doubled and heavy consonants make that undoing sound compressed and strained at the point of failure.

topics.headline: dependent self-collapse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wall’s fall remains a subordinated tendency and that the form makes the failure internal.
topics.reason: QAC marks a subjunctive Form VII verb governed by the preceding particle.

topics.headline: undoing what was bound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees collapse as the undoing of coherence, not just vertical falling.
topics.reason: V4 supports physical and covenantal undoing; local sense selects structural collapse while preserving breach imagery.

topics.headline: collapse answered by standing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the compact reversal: undoing is immediately answered by making stand.
topics.reason: Contextual rows pair the collapse root with the establishment root and later explanation.

topics.headline: compressed heavy collapse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears doubled and heavy consonants enact pressure at the point of structural failure.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows give concrete sound payoffs tied to collapse.

words.gloss_range: causal-sequential connector from danger to repair
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) links the wall’s danger directly to repair. The ayah again uses action adjacency rather than explanation: the wall tends toward collapse, so al-Khiḍr acts, with no negotiation, request, or payment discussion before the intervention. As the fourth stacked connector, its clipped onset keeps the problem-to-solution turn sharp and immediate.

topics.headline: immediate repair consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the repair follows directly from the wall’s condition.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence license the connector between the collapse tendency and repair verb.

topics.headline: then-so repair force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees sequence and causality working together in the move from problem to solution.
topics.reason: The particle force locally supports both nextness and consequence.

topics.headline: fourth action-chain connector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the stacked connectors making the ayah move by linked actions rather than commentary.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows count the repeated connectors and identify the repair hinge.

topics.headline: sharp repair onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the clipped connector and onset match the immediacy of intervention.
topics.reason: The phonetic row provides the concrete acoustic payoff.

words.gloss_range: singular Form IV act of making the wall stand again
words.root_gloss_range: standing, establishing, straightening, restoration, uprightness, and value; locally causative restoration is selected
words.prose: {{ar:أَقَامَهُۥ}} ({{tr:aqāmahu}}) interrupts the dual chain with singular agency: al-Khiḍr alone makes the same wall stand. The suffix returns to the endangered wall, and Form IV selects causative restoration rather than new construction or appraisal. The standing-root reverses the collapse-root, while its value field makes Musa’s later wage objection linguistically available; the act remains underexplained until (18:82) discloses why this standing mattered. The q-m articulation gives the repair a firm close that matches the stabilizing action.

topics.headline: singular repair agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the agency split: both saw the wall, but al-Khiḍr alone restores it.
topics.reason: QAC marks a singular perfect Form IV verb with a suffix referring back to the wall.

topics.headline: causative standing restoration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the action as making an existing wall stand again, not simply building a new structure.
topics.reason: V4 supports standing, establishing, straightening, and value; local form selects causative restoration.

topics.headline: unpaid counter-action after refusal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices al-Khiḍr supplying restorative action where the town withheld hospitality, with the reason deferred to (18:82).
topics.reason: Contextual rows connect refusal, establishment, reward, and the later explanatory disclosure.

topics.headline: firm repair closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the firm sound of the verb fit the act of stabilizing the wall.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a concrete sound payoff for the repair action.

words.gloss_range: completed speech verb introducing Musa’s protest
words.root_gloss_range: saying, speaking, declaring, asserting; locally a spoken objection is selected
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) shifts the ayah from silent repair into Musa’s evaluation. The subject is unexpressed but recoverable from the protest pattern, and the speech act itself becomes the third breach of the patience agreement. Across the three incidents, departure leads to action and then Musa speaks at (18:71), (18:74), and (18:77); this final speech triggers the separation declaration in (18:78).

topics.headline: unexpressed speaker recovered
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Musa is inferred as speaker without being renamed, so narrative roles must be tracked.
topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect speech verb and context identifies Musa as the speaker.

topics.headline: speech as objection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the verb as an evaluative speech-act, not a neutral sound report.
topics.reason: V4 supports articulated saying and assertion, locally specialized as protest after repair.

topics.headline: final protest refrain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated pattern where each incident culminates in Musa’s speech, now opening the separation boundary.
topics.reason: Contextual rows connect the speech verb to the three incident refrains at (18:71), (18:74), and (18:77).

words.gloss_range: counterfactual particle opening Musa’s unrealized-payment protest
words.prose: {{ar:لَوْ}} ({{tr:law}}) opens an unreal condition: payment-taking did not happen, and Musa frames it as a missed option. The particle lets the criticism sound indirect, almost wish-like, while still organizing the whole protest as condition plus consequence. Its diphthong gives the objection a paced opening before the following glottal break, and that counterfactual complaint sets up the explanatory response promised in (18:78).

topics.headline: unreal counterfactual condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Musa presupposes payment was not taken and frames it as an unrealized possibility.
topics.reason: QAC and contextual evidence support the particle as counterfactual condition governing the final clause.

topics.headline: indirect wish-like reproach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees Musa criticizing through an unreal condition rather than issuing a direct command.
topics.reason: The particle’s counterfactual and wish-like force both fit the local protest.

topics.headline: complete protest frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final speech organized as a formal condition-response frame that demands explanation.
topics.reason: Topical rows connect the particle to the full counterfactual payment clause and next-ayah explanation.

topics.headline: paced protest opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the protest begin slowly before the following glottal break.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a concrete sound payoff.

words.gloss_range: second-person perfect volition inside the unreal condition
words.root_gloss_range: willing, choosing, and thingness; locally deliberate will is selected with possible-thing pressure
words.prose: {{ar:شِئْتَ}} ({{tr:shiʾta}}) puts the unrealized choice directly on al-Khiḍr: had he willed, the payment-taking would have followed. The perfect form seals that will inside the counterfactual as a completed non-choice, not a live request. The root’s will-and-thing range makes the omitted wage a possible thing not brought into action, and the wording narrows Surah 18’s larger will discourse from divine-dependent action at (18:23) and (18:24) and Musa’s patience at (18:69) to this human economic choice. The glottal stop arrests the word just where Musa names will.

topics.headline: addressed perfect volition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Musa directly assigns the missed option to al-Khiḍr’s will.
topics.reason: QAC marks a second-person masculine singular perfect verb inside the counterfactual frame.

topics.headline: will making a possible thing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees payment as something al-Khiḍr could have willed into action but did not.
topics.reason: V4 supports will and thingness, while local sense selects volitional choice.

topics.headline: human will within Surah will discourse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contrast between broader divine-will discourse and this narrower human wage choice, including (18:23) and (18:24) and (18:69).
topics.reason: Contextual rows connect the will root to Surah 18’s local will field.

topics.headline: glottal break at will
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears an audible arrest at the word where Musa names will.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a concrete sound payoff.

words.gloss_range: apodosis marker binding unreal condition to consequence
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) marks the second half of Musa’s counterfactual: had the will occurred, then payment-taking would have followed. Because it fuses into the following verb, logical dependency becomes visible and audible as a prefix, strengthening Musa’s claim that the consequence was definite under the unreal condition.

topics.headline: counterfactual answer marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the formal hinge that completes the condition-response construction.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as the answer lām of the counterfactual apodosis.

topics.headline: answer plus emphasis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the consequence both identified and strengthened by the same bound particle.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows support both answer-marker and emphatic force.

topics.headline: second half of protest frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final protest becoming formally complete before the taking verb lands.
topics.reason: Topical rows pair this particle with the opening counterfactual particle.

topics.headline: fused consequence sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the marker pronounced into the taking verb it governs.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives the concrete audible binding payoff.

words.gloss_range: perfect Form VIII taking imagined as unreal completed wage-claim
words.root_gloss_range: taking, seizing, adopting, and claiming; locally self-directed compensation-claim is selected, not forceful seizure
words.prose: {{ar:ٱتَّخَذْتَ}} ({{tr:ittakhadhta}}) is the unreal consequence Musa imagines as already complete under the counterfactual. Form VIII makes the taking self-directed and purposeful: not seizure by force, but claiming compensation for oneself. The fused prefix tightens condition and consequence, while the same taking root will contrast with the king’s seizure of ships in (18:79); Musa’s proposed taking is economic and reactive, not royal confiscation. The doubled taking sound gives the imagined claim a compressed force without changing it into coercion.

topics.headline: unreal completed taking consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wage-taking is imagined as a completed result that did not occur.
topics.reason: QAC marks a perfect second-person verb in the counterfactual apodosis, with the prefixed marker fused to it.

topics.headline: self-directed compensation claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees Musa proposing a personal claim to payment, not violent seizure.
topics.reason: V4 root range includes seizing and adopting, while local Form VIII and wage object narrow the sense to compensation-claim.

topics.headline: repair reframed as transaction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repair being reclassified as work that could have yielded compensation, with contrast to (18:79) taking.
topics.reason: Contextual rows connect the taking verb to wage, Musa’s reactive speech, and the later king scene at (18:79).

topics.headline: forceful doubled taking sound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the compressed doubled sound match the pressure of claiming payment.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a concrete sound payoff for the taking verb.

words.gloss_range: prepositional basis for the imagined wage
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}) gives the basis for the wage before the wage itself appears. Its suffix can point to the wall, the repair, or the responsible party, so Musa’s proposal remains broad: payment could be for the object, for the work, or upon someone connected with it. The preposition carries exchange and obligation pressure together, keeping the repair tightly attached to compensation, and the glide-to-hamza boundary into the next word marks the audible turn toward payment.

topics.headline: elastic suffix basis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the payment basis is compressed into a suffix with several local referent options.
topics.reason: QAC marks a preposition with a masculine suffix referring back into the repair scene.

topics.headline: exchange and obligation pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the payment as both compensation for work and potentially something owed.
topics.reason: The preposition’s local range supports for-it and upon-it pressures.

topics.headline: basis before wage object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ground of compensation is heard before the wage lands as final object.
topics.reason: Topical rows identify the prepositional phrase as preceding and preparing the wage.

topics.headline: break into payment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the boundary into the wage word mark the turn to compensation.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a concrete sound transition.

words.gloss_range: indefinite compensation as final object of the protest
words.root_gloss_range: reward, wage, recompense, fee, and making-whole pressure; locally open-ended compensation is selected
words.prose: {{ar:أَجْرًۭا}} ({{tr:ajran}}) closes the ayah as the object Musa says could have been taken. Its indefiniteness leaves payer, amount, and kind unspecified, so the issue is compensation in principle rather than a fixed price. The root ranges from divine reward to human wage and can carry restoration imagery, making the word apt after the wall is set upright; as the final word, it gathers need, unpaid repair, and Musa’s economic reading, and it triggers the separation speech in (18:78). The final tanwīn gives that unspecified compensation a clear closing cadence.

topics.headline: indefinite final wage object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that payment is the last object of the protest and remains unspecified.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as indefinite accusative object of the taking verb.

topics.headline: reward-wage and making-whole range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the term as broader than a fixed hire price, with restoration pressure after the wall repair.
topics.reason: V4 supports reward, wage, compensation, and restoration imagery; local speech narrows it to proposed human compensation.

topics.headline: closing compensation pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah’s movement from hungry need to imagined payment for work, making economic objection the final pressure.
topics.reason: Contextual rows connect the final wage to Surah reward language, opening need, and next-ayah separation.

topics.headline: indefinite closing cadence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final tanwīn leave compensation unspecified while closing the ayah.
topics.reason: The phonetic row gives a concrete closing-sound payoff.

baseline_models.mechanism: The settlement lexeme joins a gathered people to the specific practice of feeding a guest; the food request activates that practice, and the inhabitants collectively refuse it.

activation_trace.role: A village is literally a gathering of people, supplying the collective body that acts.
Feeding a guest from gathered food is a village-root image, making hospitality an internal function of the named settlement.
Requesting that another provide food supplies the explicit demand placed on that communal function.
Severe refusal blocks acceptance of the request and turns omission into an active communal stance.
A traveler descending upon others as a guest specifies the relation the inhabitants decline.

changed_reading.before: Two travelers encounter an inhospitable town.
changed_reading.after: A gathered settlement refuses a guest-feeding function already latent in its own designation, so its social coherence fails at the point of hospitality.

baseline_models.mechanism: The sequence moves from an unbound construction to uprightness, valuation, and compensation. Since أجر also images mending a crooked fracture, the repair has already materialized one kind of ajr before Musa proposes taking another.

activation_trace.role: Undoing a bound or built structure supplies the wall's imminent structural failure.
Straightness and equilibrium supply the physical result of setting the wall right.
Valuation and pricing turn the same restoration into work that can be appraised.
Acquiring something for oneself supplies Musa's proposed conversion of the deed into income.
Payment for work supplies the ordinary economic reading of the proposed wage.
Mending a fracture that healed crookedly folds the wall's rectification back into the wage lexeme.

changed_reading.before: Khidr repairs a wall gratuitously, and Musa suggests charging for the work.
changed_reading.after: The repair and the proposed wage mirror one another: the wall is straightened, valued, and already given the fracture-mending image carried by ajr, while monetary ajr remains untaken.

baseline_models.mechanism: The wall's attributed desire can be read as compressed material diagnosis: oscillation and load-strain announce failure, while iqama answers with support, preservation, and restored standing.

activation_trace.role: The elevated wall supplies the built body whose standing is at issue.
Back-and-forth movement and failure to settle give the wall's 'wanting' a visible wobble.
Joints or a back creaking under weight give impending collapse an audible strain signal.
Care, preservation, and oversight make setting upright an act of guardianship as well as mechanics.
A supporting mainstay supplies the counterforce that keeps the diagnosed structure standing.

changed_reading.before: The wall's desire is decorative personification meaning that collapse is near.
changed_reading.after: Its 'desire' renders physical instability legible: wobble and strain solicit a preserving support response.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus repair becomes the third opaque intervention in a repeated journey sequence. The first two look destructive and the third constructive, yet all three resist judgment from visible effect until their outcomes are disclosed.

activation_trace.role: Preserving care anchors the apparently benevolent third intervention in the focus.
Complete cognitive enclosure supplies the knowledge Musa lacks when judging each intervention.
Knowledge of an affair's interior supplies the hidden layer unavailable at first sight.
A literal breach supplies the first intervention's visibly destructive pole.
Taking life supplies the second and most severe visibly destructive pole.
Return to an eventual outcome supplies the deferred horizon on which all three acts become readable.

structural_cues: 18:71, 18:74, and 18:77 repeat فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰ إِذَا, each followed by an intervention and an objection; 18:78 defers explanation until after the third.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated frame, two destructive surfaces, one constructive surface, and deferred outcomes; I infer one diagnostic series in which visible moral polarity is unreliable. A live alternative is that the repetition marks itinerary without making the three acts functionally symmetric.

changed_reading.before: The wall repair is straightforward kindness after two shocking acts.
changed_reading.after: The repair is the third epistemic test case: even a visibly good act conceals its beneficiary, timing, and governing reason.

context_deltas.mechanism: The wall functions as temporary guardianship: standing masonry keeps stored wealth unavailable while its owners lack a guardian, then yields its contents only after they reach strength. Repair preserves both value and timing.

activation_trace.role: An elevated wall supplies the physical barrier whose continued standing can protect what lies below.
Care and guardianship turn structural repair into surrogate custody.
A mainstay that keeps something standing supplies the material means of that custody.
Children cut off from their guardian supply the vulnerable beneficiaries for whom the wall stands in.
Preserved stored wealth supplies the value held behind the standing barrier.
Arrival at an endpoint supplies the delay's terminating condition.
Attaining mature strength specifies when the owners can replace the wall's guardianship.
Bringing a thing out of concealment supplies the eventual release of the protected value.
Compassion supplies the governing relation behind preservation without payment.

structural_cues: 18:82 places the treasure under the same wall, assigns it to two orphans, and sequences maturity before extraction.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies ownership, orphanhood, below-wall treasure, maturity, extraction, and mercy; I infer that continued standing delays access and substitutes for a guardian. The wall may instead be only a cover or site marker, but either alternative still makes repair preserve the release time.

changed_reading.before: Khidr keeps a failing structure upright in the present.
changed_reading.after: He installs a time-bound custodian: the wall stands for absent guardians, holding an inheritance through the owners' vulnerable interval.

context_deltas.mechanism: Musa's proposal and the ship explanation expose two economies of taking: compensation can be acquired for work, whereas a ruler takes working people's property by force. The repair remains deliberately unpriced between them.

activation_trace.role: Acquisition for oneself supplies the legitimate proposed taking attached to repair.
Payment returned for labor supplies the proposed reciprocal exchange.
A worker's wage or livelihood links the ship owners' labor to the focus proposal of earned compensation.
Taking possession supplies the ruler's competing form of acquisition.
Taking by injustice and force marks that competing acquisition as coercive rather than earned.

structural_cues: The proposed taking of a wage at 18:77 is followed in the explanation by a king who takes every ship forcibly from poor workers at 18:79.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies work, wage, two instances of taking, and coercion; I infer an ethical contrast between earned acquisition and seizure, with the untaken wage keeping the repair outside both. Alternatively, Musa may be proposing only a pragmatic way to recover food, without a broader theory of exchange.

changed_reading.before: Musa sensibly proposes payment for useful labor.
changed_reading.after: His proposal names the legitimate counterpart to predatory taking, while the actual repair declines appropriation and remains a protected transfer to unseen owners.

context_deltas.mechanism: The pair first finds a servant carrying granted mercy and knowledge, then finds a wall whose concealed yield is later extracted as stored wealth and mercy. Repeated finding shifts the wall from incidental obstacle to an encountered carrier of hidden benefit.

activation_trace.role: Coming upon the servant supplies the first discovery in the paired finding sequence.
Granted compassion supplies a hidden benefit carried by the first discovered figure.
Knowledge disclosed to a knower supplies the unseen capacity of that figure.
Coming upon the wall repeats finding but transfers the discovered object from person to structure.
Preserved hidden wealth supplies the wall's initially invisible yield.
Extraction from concealment supplies the later disclosure of what the found wall carried.

structural_cues: The same dual subject finds the servant at 18:65 and the wall at 18:77; 18:82 discloses what was hidden under the wall.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated finding, mercy and knowledge in the first encounter, and concealed wealth in the second; I infer a parallel between encountered carriers of unseen benefit. A live alternative is that وجد merely advances the itinerary and does not couple the two finds.

changed_reading.before: The pair happens upon a failing wall.
changed_reading.after: They find a second opaque carrier: the wall's visible defect masks a stored benefit just as the earlier found servant's visible presence masked granted knowledge.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it transfers a hospitality image to masonry. It remains anchored by the focus inventory's literal leaning sense for ضيف, the wall's imminent fall, and iqama as support; downstream prose should present it only as a social-material analogy, not as literal identification or causal equivalence.

activation_trace.role: A thing leaning onto another supplies the material analogue latent in refused guesting.
The elevated wall supplies the second body now unable to maintain itself.
A built structure coming undone supplies the wall's need to lean on support.
A mainstay that prevents falling supplies Khidr's reception of that structural dependence.

changed_reading.before: The refusal of guests and the repair of a wall are adjacent but unrelated events.
changed_reading.after: The people refuse the travelers who lean upon them, while Khidr receives the leaning wall by becoming its support.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because focus أَبَوْا ordinarily realizes refusal, while parental care comes from the packet's non-dominant ء ب و mapping. It remains valid as an explicitly supplied split-root activation sharpened by the father and orphans in 18:82; downstream prose must label it exploratory resonance, not derive fatherhood from the focus form.

activation_trace.role: Fatherhood as causative nurture supplies a non-dominant counterimage inside the focus refusal inventory.
Preserving care supplies the focus action through which that counterimage becomes functional.
Actual fatherhood and nurture in the explanation stabilize the packet-supplied parental branch.
Loss of a child's guardian supplies the gap through which the father's care must persist indirectly.
The father's soundness supplies the enduring moral cause attached to the children's protection.
Nurturing, repairing, and bringing to completion supplies the agency that carries parental care across absence.

changed_reading.before: Communal refusal is followed by an unexplained act of wall repair.
changed_reading.after: An exploratory split-root echo opposes failed present nurture by the town to an absent father's care, prolonged through repair until his children can receive it.

strongest_changes: The village's own branch field includes guest-feeding, so the refusal reads as failure of a constitutive communal function.
Ajr joins payment to mending a crooked fracture, making the repaired wall a material counterpart to the wage that is proposed but not taken.
The later disclosure turns upright masonry into time-bound guardianship over an inheritance and places legitimate wage-taking against coercive seizure.
summary.what_was_special: The focus lexicon cross-connects social, material, and economic mechanisms: قري gathers people and feeds guests, ضيف leans, قوم stands, guards, and values, and أجر pays while mending a crooked break. Context converts those links into deferred custody without collapsing their distinct readings.
remaining_uncertainties: The parental activation depends on the packet's non-dominant ء ب و mapping for focus ء ب ي and must remain exploratory.
The guest-wall parallel is analogical; the grammar does not identify the wall as a guest.
The wall may be cover, marker, or container; the packet supports temporal protection more strongly than any single physical mechanism.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Refused hospitality makes wage-taking appear causally apt.** `ش ي ء` B001’s “willing” variant governs Moses’ alternative, and `ق و ل` B001 externalizes it after unpaid repair. The later explanation reveals absent orphan beneficiaries and paternal soundness (18:82). I infer that visible social reciprocity suggests extracting payment from the village, while hidden intergenerational reciprocity directs free preservation. The ayah contrasts immediate exchange with delayed care.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:82 revealed orphan protection and paternal soundness, overturning the immediate wage logic without denying village failure.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Persons refused a turn-in while a leaning wall receives support.** `ض ي ف/B002` is one who turns in as a guest, grounded in `ض ي ف/B001`, turning or leaning toward another. The villagers refuse the travelers’ turn toward them, yet the scene immediately presents a wall leaning toward collapse and being set upright; 18:82 reveals that this unpaid support protects orphan property. I infer a deliberate hospitality inversion: the wall receives the sustaining response withheld from persons, and that response benefits absent dependents. `يُضَيِّفُوهُمَا` reads as failed social load-bearing, not only refusal of food. The packet has no accepted inventory for `ق ض ض`, so no branch claim is made for `يَنقَضَّ`.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:78 announced separation, but 18:82 surprisingly showed that the unpaid wall-work was deferred hospitality for orphans rather than service to the refusing town.

baseline.text: Yine yola çıktılar. Bir kent halkına varınca onlardan yiyecek istediler, fakat halk onları ağırlamayı reddetti. Orada yıkılmak üzere olan bir duvar buldular; o da duvarı düzeltti. Musa, Dileseydin buna karşılık bir ücret alabilirdin, dedi.

findings.text: Köyün görünen karşılıksızlığı ücret istemeyi makul gösterirken, gizli yetimler ve babalarının iyiliği ücretsiz onarımı kuşaklar arası gecikmiş karşılığa yöneltir.
İki yolcu içeri alınmazken eğilmiş duvarın desteklenmesi, kişilere esirgenen ağırlamanın cansız bir yapıya verilmiş gibi görünmesini sağlar.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Straightening the wall preserves concealment. Its success consists in preventing present access until the intended beneficiaries are strong enough to open what it guards.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The whole-surah pattern places physical architecture and sensory reception under one functional test without erasing their distinct scenes.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Selective Boundaries Preserve Without Permanently Sealing
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: The cave routes light and repels intrusion, the repaired wall delays extraction until maturity, and the rampart blocks passage until the promise.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: sheltering cave `ك ه ف:B002/m01`; forecourt threshold `و ص د:B002/m01`; side-cutting passage `ق ر ض:B002/m01`; raised wall `ج د ر:B001/m01`; arrival at an endpoint `ب ل غ:B001/m01`; gap-closing barrier `س د د:B001/m01`; breach-filling construction `ر د م:B001/m01`; piercing breach `ن ق ب:B001/m01`; appointed promise `و ع د:B003/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 18:16-18 (cave refuge, routed light, threshold, and repelled observer); 18:77, 18:82 (wall, treasure, and maturity); 18:93-98 (barrier, blocked passage, and promised leveling)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: These structures regulate access for a purpose and a term. They admit sustaining influence or intended beneficiaries while excluding intrusion, predation, and premature opening.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: Compensation Shifts from Wage to Consequence
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: The return on action may appear as promised reward, negotiable wage, or proportionate consequence, but it remains tied to the action's actual function rather than immediate recognition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The unpaid wall repair separates the worth of an act from whether its nearest beneficiaries recognize or finance it.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Repair Is Performed Where Food Is Refused and Wage Is Available
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A town refuses to feed the travelers, yet its collapsing wall is repaired even though the repairer could have taken a wage.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: requested food `ط ع م:B002/m01`; earned recompense or wage `ء ج ر:B001/m01`; raised wall `ج د ر:B001/m01`; tender mercy `ر ح م:B001/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 18:77 (refused food, repaired wall, and possible wage); 18:82 (the repair disclosed as mercy)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The scene breaks reciprocity between beneficiary and worker. The repair's purpose lies with absent orphans and future maturity, not with compensation from the inhospitable town.

root_profile.summary: Kök, bağdan kurtarıp serbest bırakma çekirdeğinden evlilik bağını sona erdirme, engelsiz ilerleme, kuruluşlara bağlı açıklık, kısıtsızlık ve hayvan gütme anlamlarına açılır; ayrıca hava, doğum, bağırsak, ağrı, bitki, bağ aracı, at nişanı, hurma bakımı, zehirleme ve beden çizgileriyle ilgili uzaklaşmış adlandırmalar taşır.

root_profile.summary: Kök, gelme ve ulaştırmadan uygun yoldan işlemeye uzanan bir çekirdeğin yanında su yolu, dışarıdan gelen sel, yabancı kişi, ürün ve artış, mali ödeme, hayvan hareketi, yol, felaket, çiftleşme isteği ve etkili kişi gibi çoğu kalıba bağlı tarihsel anlam dalları taşır.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه أهل الرجل وزوجه وأخص الناس به، وسكان البيت، وأهل الدين أو النسب أو الصناعة أو البلد ومن يجمعهم مسكن أو رابطة.
يدخل فيه التأهل والتزوج، وأهل الرجل أو أهل امرأة، والدعاء بآهلك الله في الجنة أي زوجك فيها وجعل لك أهلا.
يدخل فيه فلان أهل لكذا أو خليق به، وأهل التقوى والمغفرة، وتأهيل الشخص لأمر.
يدخل فيه المكان المأهول أو الآهل، وكون الشيء أو الدابة يألف مكانا فيكون أهليا، والأنس بالإنسان أو المكان.
يدخل فيه قول مرحبا وأهلا في التحية، بمعنى وجدت سعة وأتيت أهلا لا غرباء فاستأنس ولا تستوحش.
يدخل فيه الإهالة: الألية أو الودك أو الشحم أو الزيت وما يؤتدم به، وما يعلو القدر من ودك اللحم السمين، واستأهل بمعنى أخذ الإهالة أو أكلها أو ائتدم بها.

root_profile.summary: Bu kök yakın çevre ve aidiyet topluluğu çevresinden evlenme, uygunluk, yerleşik alışma ve karşılama kalıbına uzanan ilişkili dallar taşır; ayrıca kaynakların ayrı asıl olarak verdiği yemeklik yağ anlamı bulunur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yerleşim yerini, orada toplanan insanları ve yerleşik kişiyi birlikte kapsar. Geçici çerçeve bu bağı doğru kurar; ancak şehirleri bağımsız bir temel anlam gibi sunmak yerine köy ve yerleşim çoğulunun kapsamı içinde tutmak gerekir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım hem yerleşim ve halk bildiren yalın biçimleri hem de yerleşik kişiyi göçebeyle karşılaştıran kalıbı ayrı kapsamlar olarak korur.

concept_map.definition: İnsanların bir arada yaşamak üzere toplandığı yerleşim yeri ve bu yerin topluca düşünülen halkıdır. Belirli bir karşıtlık kalıbında, böyle bir yerleşimde oturan kişi göçebeden ayrılır.

facets.statement: İnsanların toplandığı köy ya da başka bir yerleşim yerini belirtir.
Yer adından hareketle o yerin halkını veya sakinlerini topluca belirtebilir.
Belirli bir ikili kalıpta yerleşimde oturan kişi, açık arazide yaşayan göçebenin karşısına konur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar yerleşimi insanların toplandığı yer olarak açıklar ve adın hem yere hem halka uzanabildiğini gösterir. Çoğul yerleşimler, bağlamda iki belirli şehir ve yerleşik ile göçebe karşıtlığı da aynı toplu kanıt içindedir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yer adı ile o yerde yaşayan topluluğun birlikte kapsandığı branch çekirdeğini en kısa doğal biçimde verir.

error_profile.preserves: Yerleşim, insan topluluğu ve ikisi arasındaki adlandırma bağını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Küçük bir yerleşim ile sakinlerinin bağlam içinde birlikte anıldığı kullanımlara uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Yerleşim ile o yerin halkı arasındaki ilişkiyi korur.
error_profile.loses: Daha geniş yerleşim kapsamını ve yerleşik-göçebe karşıtlığını dışarıda bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yalnızca yerleşimde oturan kişi ile açık arazide yaşayan kişinin karşılaştırıldığı kalıpta kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yerleşik kişinin göçebeden ayrıldığı karşıtlığı korur.
error_profile.loses: Yerleşim yerinin ve halkının genel adlandırılmasını kapsamaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: İnsanların yaşadığı yerleşimi ve o yerin halkını adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Suyu, yiyeceği veya başka bir maddeyi bir yerde toplama ve birikme sürecini adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da ayrı öğelerin bir yerde toplanması düşüncesi bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal topluluğun yaşadığı yer ve halk için kalıcı bir adlandırmadır; komşu dal ise su veya maddeyi bir kapta, ağızda ya da yarada toplama ve birikme olayını anlatır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; yayımlanan karşılaştırma, ortak toplanma düşüncesine rağmen yerleşim adı ile maddi birikme arasındaki en yakın karışma noktasını gösterir.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه القرية للموضع الذي يجتمع فيه الناس، وللناس أنفسهم أو أهلها، والقرى والمدن، والقار في مقابلة البادي.
branches.source_phrase_ar: القرية سميت قرية لاجتماع الناس فيها (maqayis)؛ القرية معروفة والجمع القرى؛ القريتين مكة والطائف؛ جاءني كل قار وباد (sihah)؛ القرية اسم للموضع الذي يجتمع فيه الناس وللناس جميعا (mufradat)

branches.branch_image_ar: جمع ماء أو شيء في مستقر
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قري الماء في الحوض أو المقراة، ومجتمع الماء وقريانه، وجمع الشيء في الفم، وجمع البعير العلف في شدقه، واجتماع المدة في الجرح، والحوصلة التي تجمع الطعام بعلاقة الإبدال.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi konuğa iyilik etmeyi ve onu özellikle yiyecekle ağırlamayı çekirdek yapar; sunulan yemek ile bu yemek için kullanılan büyük kaplar da aynı konuk ağırlama bağlamına bağlıdır. Geçici çerçeve bu ilişkiyi doğru yansıtır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım konuk ağırlama çekirdeğini korur ve konuğu ağırlamak, sunulan yiyecek ve konuk sofrasındaki kaplar gibi kalıba bağlı kullanımları ayırır.

concept_map.definition: Bir konuğa iyilik edip onu özellikle yiyecek sunarak ağırlamaktır. Konuğa sunulan yemek ile bu amaçla kullanılan büyük servis kabı da yalnızca bu ağırlama bağlamında dala bağlıdır.

facets.statement: Konuğa iyilik etme, onu ağırlama ve özellikle doyuracak yiyecek sunma eylemidir.
Konuğa sunulan yiyecek, ağırlama eyleminin sağladığı şey olarak adlandırılır.
Konukların çevresinde toplandığı veya yemeklerinin konduğu büyük çanak ve servis kapları bu bağlama özgüdür.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıt konuğu iyi karşılayıp doyurmayı ortak çekirdek olarak verir. Konuğa sunulan yiyecek, konukların çevresinde toplandığı büyük çanak ve onların ağırlandığı kaplar bu eylemin bağlama bağlı adlandırmalarıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Konuğa iyilik etme ile yiyecek sunma bileşenlerini birlikte taşıyan en kısa doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Konuk katılımcısını, iyilik amacını ve yiyecek sunma yolunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir ev sahibinin gelen konuğa yiyecek vererek iyilik ettiği eylem cümlelerine uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Ev sahibinin konuğa yiyecek sunarak iyi davranması olayını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Eylemden çok konuğun önüne getirilen yiyeceğin adlandırıldığı bağlamda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yiyeceğin konuk ağırlama amacıyla sunulduğu bağı korur.
error_profile.loses: Ev sahibinin ağırlama eylemini ve servis kabını kapsamaz.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: konukların çevresinde toplandığı büyük yemek çanağı

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Ev sahibinin konuğa iyilik edip özellikle yiyecek sunmasını merkez alır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Konuğun gelişi, bir yere konuk olarak inmesi, birinin konuk edilmesi ve konukluk istemesi gibi daha geniş rolleri kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da ev sahibi ile konuk arasındaki ağırlama sahnesinde buluşur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal ev sahibinin yiyecek sağlayan iyiliğini adlandırır; komşu dal ise konuğun kendisini, gelişini ve konuk edilme ilişkisinin daha geniş bütününü kapsar.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; yayımlanan komşu, yiyecekle ağırlama eylemini genel konukluk ilişkisinden ayıran en yararlı sınırı sağlar.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قرى الضيف وإقراؤه، والقرى والقراء بمعنى الإحسان إليه، وما قري به الضيف من طعام أو جفنة في سياق الضيافة.
branches.source_phrase_ar: المقراة الجفنة سميت لاجتماع الضيف عليها أو لما جمع فيها من طعام (maqayis)؛ القرى الإحسان إلى الضيف؛ قراه يقريه قرى؛ المقاري جفان يقرى فيها الأضياف (ayn)؛ المقرى إناء يقرى فيه الضيف؛ قريت الضيف قرى وقراء أحسنت إليه؛ ما قري به الضيف (sihah)؛ قريت الضيف قرى (mufradat)

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه القرو والمقراة والمقرى للقدح أو الحوض أو الإناء أو الجفنة أو المسيل، وما نقر من أسفل النخلة أو كان كالمعصرة إذا كان موضع جمع.
يدخل فيه قرو البلاد أو قريها أو اقتراها أو استقراها بمعنى تتبعها أرضا بعد أرض، وسلوك القصد أو الطريق، وتتبع المياه، وقري الطريق بمعنى ناحيته أو سننه.
يدخل فيه القرو بمعنى الشيء أو القوم على طريقة واحدة، وكون الأرض قروا واحدا إذا طبقها المطر.
يدخل فيه القرا بمعنى الظهر، والناقة القرواء طويلة السنام أو شديدة الظهر.
يدخل فيه القرية بلا همز أو على فعيلة: خشبات أو عصيتان وما يعرض عليهما وفي وسطهما فرض يجعل فيه رأس عمود البيت.

branches.branch_image_ar: جمع مهموز في حمل وقرآن وقرء
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه عند ابن فارس الباب المهموز: ما قرأت الناقة سلى أي ما حملت، والقرآن لجمعه ما فيه، وأقرأت المرأة، والقرء وقت للطهر مرة وللحيض مرة، وهبوب الرياح لقارئها أي لوقتها.
يدخل فيه القارئة بمعنى الشاهد، وقوارى الله في الأرض بمعنى الشهود الذين يتتبعون الناس وأعمالهم حتى يجمعوا علما ثم يشهدوا.
يدخل فيه القرة بمعنى المال من الإبل والغنم، والقرة بمعنى العيال.
يدخل فيه القارية بمعنى طرف السنان، وحد كل شيء أو قاريته، وأعلى السنان أو حد السيف.

root_profile.summary: Kökün dalları insanların yerleşimde toplanması, maddelerin bir yerde birikmesi, konuğun yemek çevresinde ağırlanması, toplama kapları, güzergâh izleme ve tek biçim kazanma gibi birbirine uzaktan bağlı alanların yanında sırt, direk başı düzeneği, dönemsel kullanımlar, tanıklık, sürü malı veya ev halkı ve keskin uç gibi bağımsızlaşmış adlandırmaları kapsar. Düzen, ortak bir toplama ve izleme eğilimi taşıyan radyal alanlarla tarihsel ya da sözlüksel olarak ayrı duran dalları birlikte barındırır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir başkasına yenilecek şey verme ile bir başkasından kendisini doyurmasını isteme yönlerini açıkça birlikte taşır. Dalın kimliği, kişinin kendisinin yemesinden değil besini veren ile alan arasındaki aktarım ilişkisinden doğar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, başkasını besleme ve beslenmeyi isteme eylemlerini yalın dal kapsamı içinde verir; özel konuşma kalıplarını içeri almaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir başkasına yiyecek veya yenilip içilebilen besleyici bir şey vermek; ayrıca bir başkasından kendisini beslemesini istemek.

facets.statement: Bir başkasına yiyecek ya da besleyici bir şey vererek onu doyurma.
Bir başkasından yiyecek vermesini ve kendisini doyurmasını isteme.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, yenilip içilebilen bir şeyi başkasına vermeyi ve bunun istenmesini aynı aktarım alanında birleştirir. İhtiyaç sahibini doyurma bu temel ilişkinin belirgin uygulamasıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Besini verme ve karşı taraftan besin talep etme yönlerini birlikte gösteren tam kapsamlı açıklamadır.

error_profile.preserves: Veren, alan ve isteme yönleriyle besin aktarımını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Birine yiyecek ya da besleyici içecek verildiği cümlelerde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Başkasına besin verme yönünü doğal biçimde korur.
error_profile.loses: Karşı taraftan besin isteme yönünü göstermez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dalda istenen şey özellikle beslenmedir ve ayrıca başkasını doyurma eylemi de bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal herhangi bir şeyi arama, isteme veya onun peşine düşme anlamını taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dalda da bir gereksinimin karşı taraftan istenmesi bulunabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Buradaki isteme besinle sınırlıdır ve besin verme karşılığını da kapsar; komşu ise nesnesi sınırlanmamış genel bir arama ve isteme alanıdır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Adayların tümü karşılaştırıldı; genel isteme alanıyla kurulan ayrım, besin aktarımına özgü katılımcı yapısını en açık biçimde gösterir.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه أطعمته الطعام واستطعمه أي سأله أن يطعمه وإطعام المحتاج
branches.source_phrase_ar: الإطعام يقع في كل ما يطعم (maqayis)؛ استطعمه سأله أن يطعمه وأطعمته الطعام (sihah)؛ استطعمه فأطعمه وأطعموا القانع ويطعمون الطعام (mufradat)

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه استطعمني الحديث وإذا استطعمكم الإمام فأطعموه أي استفتح فافتحوا عليه أو لقنوه
يدخل فيه الطاعم حسن الحال والمطعم المرزوق والمطعام كثير القرى والطعمة مأكلة أو وجه مكسب أو ضيعة أو فيء وخراج
يدخل فيه أطعمت النخلة أو الثمرة إذا أدرك ثمرها أو أخذت الطعم، وكل شيء وجد طعمه، واللبن المطعم والشجر المثمر
يدخل فيه القوس المطعمة والجوارح أو الإصبع المطعمة وما يطعم صاحبه الصيد أو يكون مرزوقا منه
يدخل فيه المطعم من الإبل إذا وجد في مخه طعم الشحم وشاة أو ناقة أو جزور طعوم أو طعيم في السمن
يدخل فيه ذو طعم أي ذو عقل وحزم، وما بفلان طعم أي لا عقل ولا حراك أو لا قيمة، ولا يطعم أي لا يتأدب ولا ينجع فيه الإصلاح
يدخل فيه مستطعم الفرس وهو ما تحت مرسنه إلى جحافله أو جحافله، واستطعمت الفرس إذا طلبت جريه
يدخل فيه إطعام الغصن إذا وصل به غصن من غير شجره فقبل الوصل، وإطعام العين قذى فطعمته
يدخل فيه الطعم بمعنى القدرة، طعمت عليه أي قدرت عليه
يدخل فيه أخذ بمطعمة فلان أي أخذ بحلقه يعصره عند الخنق والقتال
يدخل فيه التطاعم أي إدخال الفم في الفم كما يفعل الحمام عند التقبيل
يدخل فيه متطاعم الخلق أي متتابع الخلق
